data.title: Zuckerberg, Musk make plea at G20 for more AI data centers
data.description: CHAPEL HILL (UNITED STATES) - Mark Zuckerberg and Elon Musk on Tuesday stressed the need for more AI data centers and the electric power needed to support them at a meeting of G20 technology ministers focused on the disruptions and opportunity brought by artificial intelligence.

data.title: Canadian minister says Russia's G20 presence sparked 'discomfort'
data.description: ASHEVILLE (UNITED STATES) - Canadian Finance Minister Francois-Philippe Champagne said Tuesday that his Russian counterpart's presence at US-hosted G20 talks has caused unease among participants, given the suffering of Ukraine since Moscow's 2022 invasion.

data.title: US defends Trump's Venezuela oil deal
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US officials on Tuesday defended President Donald Trump's oil deal with Venezuela, saying it would lower oil prices for Americans and counter Russian and Chinese influence on Washington's doorstep.

data.title: Norway's King Haakon VIII swears allegiance to constitution
data.description: OSLO - Norway's King Haakon VIII took an oath before parliament on Tuesday, the first major institutional step of his reign, though his wife, still convalescing after a lung transplant, was unable to attend.

data.title: Back-to-school in Cuba a grim day with shortages of everything
data.description: HAVANA - Cuban children began the new school year Tuesday with shortages of teachers, food and uniforms -- and often no electricity -- as the island endures a crippling US pressure campaign.

data.title: Syria site infrastructure 'consistent with nuclear reactor': IAEA
data.description: VIENNA - A Syrian site held infrastructure "consistent with a nuclear reactor", the UN nuclear watchdog said in a confidential report seen by AFP on Tuesday, adding that the country under ousted former leader Bashar al-Assad "failed to report nuclear material, facilities and activities".

data.title: Nepali families hold symbolic funerals for the missing
data.description: KATHMANDU - After days of searching shelters and morgues, many Nepali families held symbolic funeral ceremonies on Tuesday to “liberate the souls” of loved ones missing since the deadly flash floods last week.

data.title: China’s Xi visits Egypt as US sanctions threat looms
data.description: BEIJING - Chinese President Xi Jinping is set to arrive in Egypt on Tuesday, making a rare trip to the Middle East as both countries face the threat of US sanctions over financial links to Iran.

data.title: Women face hygiene woes in Nepal flood relief camp
data.description: NUWAKOT, Nepal - Scores of women queued at a school sheltering Nepal flood victims, jostling to lreceive personal-care supplies, as concerns over sanitation and menstrual hygiene mount days after the catastrophic disaster.

data.title: Ukraine’s defences, ‘hybrid’ threat from Moscow headline EU talks
data.description: WICKLOW, Ireland - EU defence ministers grappled on Tuesday with bolstering Ukraine’s air defences, as worries grow over Russia’s campaign to destabilise Kyiv’s European backers.

data.title: Tibet activists accuse China of downplaying floods
data.description: DHARAMSALA, India - Exiled Tibetans and advocacy groups have accused China of heavily underreporting the death toll from devastating flooding in border regions with Nepal, claims Beijing rejected as “malicious smearing and sensationalism”.

data.title: Japan to relax overtime regulation under workaholic PM
data.description: TOKYO — Japan will ease overtime regulation starting Tuesday in a move meant to help spur economic growth but criticised as a relapse into the country's ingrained workaholic culture.

data.title: Afghanistan war victims left 'without justice', UN says
data.description: KABUL - Most civilian victims of Afghanistan's 2001-2021 war have been left "without justice, reparation or even acknowledgement" of their suffering, the United Nations (UN) said Tuesday, with one man in Kabul telling Agence France-Presse ( AFP ) "the world has forgotten us".

data.title: Iran president offers US olive branch before Putin meeting
data.description: BISHKEK (KYRGYZSTAN) - Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian on Tuesday vowed to match any US move to return to a June deal aimed at ending their war, as he prepares to meet Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin at a regional summit.

data.title: China-Nepal flood toll tops 1,000 as tunnel rescue offers last hope
data.description: NUWAKOT — The death toll from devastating Himalayan glacial floods crossed the grim 1,000 mark on Tuesday, as Chinese and Nepali teams searched for survivors including dozens feared trapped in hydropower tunnels.

data.title: Nepal's wall of missing offers last hope after Himalayan flood
data.description: KATHMANDU — In Nepal's capital, desperate people searching for family members missing after Wednesday's devastating floods post photographs on a wall, clinging to a final, fading hope of finding them.

data.title: Defence tech hub Munich booms as Europe rearms
data.description: MUNICH — Munich is booming as a hub for young defence tech firms making everything from AI-powered drones to cutting-edge military software as Europe rearms to face an increasingly dangerous world.

data.title: Nigeria rethinks criminalisation of suicide
data.description: LAGOS - In Nigeria, surviving a suicide attempt can mean facing not only the trauma of the ordeal but also the threat of prosecution.

data.title: 'Massive' Russian missile, drone attack on Kyiv kills 8
data.description: KYIV (UKRAINE) - A "massive" Russian attack killed at least eight people in Kyiv overnight, including seven at a railways depot, officials said Tuesday, as Moscow pressed its air campaign on the Ukrainian capital and surrounding areas.

data.title: US teen charged with aiding mosque shooters share livestream, manifesto
data.description: NORTH CAROLINA — A jury charged a teen in the US state of North Carolina on Monday with allegedly aiding two other teenagers livestream their shooting rampage of a mosque on the other side of the country in May.

data.title: US Army Secretary Driscoll submits resignation: White House
data.description: WASHINGTON — US Army Secretary Dan Driscoll has submitted his resignation, the White House confirmed Monday, following reports of tensions with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

data.title: China-Taiwan friction clouds Pacific summit
data.description: KOROR — Australia said Tuesday the Pacific bloc will decide for itself who attends its annual summit, after China raised objections to Taiwan's presence on the sidelines.

data.title: Boat builders keep Pakistan's fishing heritage afloat
data.description: KARACHI - The rhythmic hammering of nails and the whine of saws echo around a coastal Karachi neighbourhood, where small figures of men work atop massive wooden fishing hulls that loom beneath a pale summer sky.

data.title: Two dead after stabbing in New York's Times Square
data.description: NEW YORK - A knife-wielding woman stabbed and killed a person and injured another in New York's tourist-filled Times Square on Monday, before she was shot and killed by police.

data.title: Middle East war a boon for UAE defence giant with global ambitions
data.description: ABU DHABI - In the heart of the Abu Dhabi desert, workers toil inside warehouses assembling drones and missiles for the UAE's Edge group, riding high on a wave of new demand for its weapons battle-tested by the Middle East war.

data.title: International news  | Bangkok Post
data.description: International news  | Bangkok Post

data.title: US Supreme Court allows Trump ballroom project to proceed
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - The US Supreme Court on Monday allowed President Donald Trump to continue construction of his White House ballroom, granting him a major victory against opponents of the project.

data.title: Trump says AI data center opponents want to be 'backwards and poor'
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - US President Donald Trump on Monday attacked opponents of artificial intelligence data centers, saying they would end up "backwards and poor" and were helping rival China.

data.title: Galliano pulls Met Gala exhibit after antisemitism backlash
data.description: NEW YORK - Top fashion designer John Galliano announced Monday he was cancelling an exhibition of his work that was to kick off New York's Met Gala next spring, following criticism from donors and political leaders over his past antisemitic remarks.

data.title: Trump says US reviewing position on Falkland Islands
data.description: WASHINGTON (UNITED STATES) - President Donald Trump said Monday that the United States is reviewing its position on the Falkland Islands, after reports that Washington threatened to oppose Britain's sovereignty if it does not increase defense spending.

data.title: Kyiv orders heightened security amid intense Russian drone strikes
data.description: KYIV (UKRAINE) - Ukraine on Monday announced stricter security protocols for Kyiv public transport, schools and even parliament amid a major surge in Russian drone attacks it says are aimed at "paralysing" the Ukrainian capital.

data.title: Jury begins deliberations in Tupac Shakur murder trial
data.description: LAS VEGAS - A jury began deliberations on Monday in the trial of a former Los Angeles gang leader accused of involvement in the sensational murder three decades ago of chart-topping rapper Tupac Shakur.

data.title: Tribunal says India cannot withdraw from water treaty with Pakistan
data.description: THE HAGUE - An international tribunal ordered India on Monday to "observe its obligations" under a treaty with Pakistan on the sharing of the Indus and other rivers, which the New Delhi government sought to suspend.

data.title: Japan's oldest person, 115-year-old woman from Nara Prefecture, dies
data.description: KYODO — Japan's oldest person, Shigeko Kagawa, a 115-year-old resident of Nara Prefecture, western Japan, died late last week, the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare reported on Monday.
